descript.abstract: A digital version of the 1:24,000-scale geologic map (AUTHOR(S), YYYY) of the area represented by the QUAD NAME 7.5-minute quadrangle. Staff at the Geological Survey of Alabama (GSA) digitized the map into vector lines, points, and polygons, and populated the nonspatial tables into the U.S. Geological Survey Geologic Mapping Schema (GeMS) format, and the content is as faithful as possible to the original map. No changes (beyond symbology) were made to the data on account of more recent information. The differences in map symbology between the publication and the GeMS data release are not considered reinterpretations of the geology and are due to improved symbology available. The style file provided in this data package is largely adapted from the FGDC Digital Cartographic Standard for Geologic Map Symbolization (USGS Techniques and Methods 11-A2, 2006) and can be applied using the value in the Symbol field; symbol and type values were assigned using information given in the report when available. Other updates to the map data could be due to cartographic errors from when the plate was constructed and are not revisions of the geology. This GeMS database was funded in part by the U.S. Geological Survey National Cooperative Geologic Mapping Program (NCGMP) under STATEMAP award number G24AC00520, program year 2024. descript.purpose: This database represents a geologic mapping project conducted by the Geological Survey of Alabama (GSA) to produce basic geologic data for use by the public, industry, and government in the area represented by the QUAD NAME 7.5-minute quadrangle. This dataset contains the geologic data from the published plate with the description of map units, a glossary a terms, and data sources encoded into tables. The geologic data in this dataset contains feature-level metadata that describes the geologic data point, polygon, and line represented and their location confidences, symbol, source, and descriptions. The Geological Survey of Alabama (GSA), established in 1848, provides service and information to Alabama and its citizens as a natural resource data gathering and research agency. As part of its mission, GSA explores and evaluates the mineral, water, energy, biological, and other natural resources of the State of Alabama and conducts basic and applied research in these fields.
descript.supplinf: CUSTOMIZE GDB NAME AL_DecaturQS035_1.0 is a composite geodataset that conforms to GeMS (Geologic Map Schema)--a standard format for the digital publication of geologic maps", available at http://ngmdb.usgs.gov/Info/standards/GeMS/. Metadata records associated with each element within the geodataset contain more detailed descriptions of their purposes, constituent entities, and attributes.). These metadata were prepared with the aid of script gems_metadata.py, version of 5/15/25. The geodatabase contains the following non-spatial tables: Data Sources, DescriptionOfMapUnits, Glossary, and GeoMaterialDict, LIST OF FEATURE CLASSES NEED TO BE CUSTOMIZED PER MAP and the feature dataset Geologic Map contains the feature classes: CartographicLines, CartographicPoints, ContactsAndFaults, GeologicPoints, MapUnitPolys, OrientationPoints, and OverlayPoints.

idinfo.useconst: Any digital or hardcopies utilizing these datasets shall clearly indicate their source: The Geological Survey of Alabama Geologic Investigations Program. The Geological Survey of Alabama should be acknowledged as the originator of the data. This dataset is to be used as a primary reference source. If the data are modified in any way by the user, the user is obligated to describe the types of modifications performed in the digital version via metadata or on the hardcopy map. The user specifically agrees not to misrepresent this dataset, nor to imply that any changes made by the user were approved by the Geological Survey of Alabama. This is public information and may be interpreted by organizations or others based on needs; however, users are responsible for the appropriate application. Federal, state, or local regulatory bodies are not to reassign to the originators any authority for decisions they make. Photographic or digital enlargement of these maps to scales greater than those at which they were originally delineated can cause misrepresentation of the data. Uses of this digital geologic map should not violate the spatial resolution of the data. Although the digital form of the data removes the constraint imposed by the scale of a paper map, the detail and accuracy inherent in map scale are also present in the digital data. The fact that this database was edited for a scale of 1:24,000 means that higher resolution information is not present in the dataset. Plotting at scales larger than 1:24,000 will not yield greater real detail, although it may reveal fine-scale irregularities below the intended resolution of the database. Similarly, where this database is used in combination with other data of higher resolution, the resolution of the combined output will be limited by the lower resolution of these data. Digital data files are periodically updated. Files are dated and or versioned, and users are responsible for obtaining the latest version of the data.

dataqual.logic: Topology is consistent with the requirements of GeMS (https://doi.org/10.3133/tm11B10). Topology rules include lines must not overlap, self-overlap, self-intersect, and be single part; and polygons must not overlap, or have gaps; and the MapUnitPolys polygon boundaries must be covered by the ContactsAndFaults lines. Water boundaries were traced from the source map and does not reflect current conditions.
dataqual.complete: This geodatabase passed Level 3 GeMS database validation, which checks attribute completeness, topology, primary key and foreign key uniqueness, and that all relevant terms are defined and cited. The GeMS toolbox is available here: https://github.com/usgs/gems-tools. The geodatabase was checked against the publication to ensure that all geologic features were included.

horizpa.horizpar: Estimated accuracy of horizontal location is given on a per-feature basis by attribute LocationConfidenceMeters. Values are expected to be correct within a factor of 2. A LocationConfidenceMeters value of -9 or -9999 indicates that no value has been assigned.

procstep.procdesc: Scans of historical paper and digital map files were georeferenced to the USGS 7.5-minute grid, the contacts were digitized, smoothed, then densified. The polygons were created using the feature to polygon tool. All point, line, and polygon data on the map plate was encoded into a GeMS database and validated using the GeMS toolbox based on the requirements at the time (2026). This data set is a digital reproduction of the quadrangle series map where no changes (beyond symbology) were made to the data on account of more recent information.
